## Design

### 2026-10-07 – Okay it was my first time doing hardware so it took me a lot of time to figure out the software, install the footprint libraries and .sym etc etc. While the kicad software seemed easy, it was actually

**1.5h**

Okay it was my first time doing hardware so it took me a lot of time to figure out the software, install the footprint libraries and .sym etc etc. While the kicad software seemed easy, it was actually quite overwhelming at first. But eventually after watching yt videos and tuts and following the hack club starbie guide, i eventually got the hang of the software.

Here's what i did in this session:
1) Installed and set-up the software and got my hands dirty with it
2) Learnt how to place components, change values and how to add nets
3) MADE THE SCHEMATIC OF STARBIE
4) Learnt how to assign footprints and also did that.

Some problems i faced:
1) I faced a ton of problems while importing the footprint libraries and assigning them
2) My Software crashed but luckily i saved my progress beforehand
3) I misclicked again and again and had to watch a ton of videos to get the hang of the software

Overall it was kinda tough but fun at the same time, looking forward to complete these projects soon

### 2026-10-07 – So I finally started building the pcb from the schematic, and it genuinly overwhelmed me more than the schematic one. However, I watched 2-3 videos and followed the week one guide of Starbie. And it e

**1.7h**

So I finally started building the pcb from the schematic, and it genuinly overwhelmed me more than the schematic one. However, I watched 2-3 videos and followed the week one guide of Starbie. And it eventually helped me lead my way to routing the pcb. Now I tried to design it to be more pretty however errors bombarded my way and most of them are still unfixed and I'm on the way to fix them. I searched through reddit, google and more sites to get help.

Some more problems that i faced were i tried to add text but i chose the wrong layer (which is edge.cuts) and i got to know about it after i ran drc (hoping that it would just run fine and i would've have completed my first pcb but NOO!! :cryin: )

Then i searched google on how to change the layer of the text and did it but its still showing some more errors whose names i dont recall correctly but it was something related to size and layers i think.

That was pretty much it, it took me a hell lot of time to figure out the pcb editor, routing and more stuff but to be very honest, its also very fun as well.

### 2026-10-08 – Ok so after tinkering around for almost an hour, i got to know that my pcb is finally routed and technically it should work now. The errors came down, the problems i faced were i had left some open wi

**0.7h**

Ok so after tinkering around for almost an hour, i got to know that my pcb is finally routed and technically it should work now. The errors came down, the problems i faced were i had left some open wire (i think that's whats it called, but those red and blue lines is what im referring to here). So i looked up some tutorials and searched some google for it and eventually fixed it. Now i still have many warnings related to cosmetic text i wanted to put up on the board and in next session im prolly going to fix it as well and will probably try to make it more cooler. I kept the pcb's shape a simple rectangle because i did not know how to draw a good star in edge.cuts

That was pretty much it for the session, and im continuing the session and i'll try to make it another shape since i have pushed the previous working pcb to github, and i'll try to make it even more cooler and after that i'll write the code/firmware for it as i DO have some experience with esp32's and C++ (including arduino ide and platform io as well)

### 2026-10-08 – I thought there was some problems in my pcb as some of the pins of my display were left unconnected and the pcb router didn't show any pad to connect it to, so i tried to sanity check it in #half-life

**1.2h**

I thought there was some problems in my pcb as some of the pins of my display were left unconnected and the pcb router didn't show any pad to connect it to, so i tried to sanity check it in #half-life-help, but i got no response, so i tried gemini and it told me that its weird and shouldn't happen, then i eventually stumbled to net labels again and it told me that i apparently had messed up the schematic so i fixed it and used the net labels correctly, it took me a lot of time to figure out what was happening.

I Also Got to know about those "Blue crosses" in the guide added to unused pins. I got to know that they are called No connect Flags and it should be added to unused pins because  Electrical Rules Checker (ERC) (i have no idea what that is) will throw a warning because it thinks you might have forgotten to wire it.
